{{nihongo|'''Iizuna Shrine'''|飯縄神社}} is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|abstract|Q845945|ar|جينجا|arz|ضريح شنتو|bcl|Shinto shrine|ca|Jinja|cs|Šintoistická svatyně|da|Shinto-tempel|de|Shintō-Schrein|el|Σιντοϊστικό Ιερό|eo|Ŝintoa sanktejo|es|Jinja|eu|Jinja|fa|معبد شینتویی|fi|Šintolainen pyhäkkö|fr|Sanctuaire shinto|hi|शिंतो मंदिर|hr|Šintoistički hram|hu|Sintó szentély|id|Jinja|it|Jinja|ja|神社|ka|ძინძია|ko|신사 (신토)|lb|Shintō-Schräin|mr|शिंतो मंदिर|nl|Jinja (heiligdom)|no|Jinja|or|ଜିଞ୍ଜା|pl|Jinja|pt|Templo xintoísta|ru|Дзиндзя|sc|Jinja|simple|Shinto shrine|sl|Šintoistično svetišče|sr|Шинтоистички храм|sv|Jinja|th|ศาลเจ้าชินโต|tok|tomo sewi pi nasin sewi Sinto|tr|Şinto tapınağı|uk|Святилище (синто)|uz|Dzindzya|vi|Thần xã|wuu|神社|zh|神社|zh_yue|神社|qid=Q845945}} located in Tomita, {{ill|Nagano (city)|Q128849|qid=Q128849}}, {{ill|Nagano Prefecture|Q127877|qid=Q127877}}. It is the {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=main shrine}} (sōsha) of the Iizuna Shrines enshrined throughout Japan.<ref>[http://www.iizuna-jinnjya.jp/goaisatu.htm Iizuna Shrine Official Website]</ref> Under the {{ill|Q712534|lt=shrine ranks}}, it was classified as a former {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=gōsha}}. {{nihongo|'''Iizuna Shrine'''|飯縄神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Shinano Province]].

== History ==
* Around the year 270, {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Ōtoji no Mikoto}} was enshrined on the summit of {{ill|Mount Iizuna|Q11666652|qid=Q11666652}} as a {{ill|Tenjin|Q1305727|qid=Q1305727}}, and the deity was called {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Iizuna Daimyōjin}}.<ref>[http://www.iizuna-jinnjya.jp/yuisyo.htm Iizuna Shrine: Origins]</ref>
* The honji (original Buddhist form) was identified as {{ill|Vairocana|Q239847|qid=Q239847}}. In {{ill|848|Q30380|qid=Q30380}} (the first year of {{ill|Kashō|Q1373157|qid=Q1373157}}), an ascetic scholar entered Mount Iizuna in {{ill|March|Q110|qid=Q110}} and beheld the revered form of the Buddha.
* In {{ill|1233|Q5421|qid=Q5421}} (the first year of {{ill|Tenpuku|Q1194452|qid=Q1194452|lt=Tenpuku}}), {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Itō Hyōbu Dayū Buzen no Kami Tadanetsuna}}, the {{ill|Jitō|Q1329805|qid=Q1329805}} of Ogino in {{ill|Shinano Province|Q289250|qid=Q289250}} ({{ill|Shinshūshinmachi|Q1042382|qid=Q1042382}}), entered the mountain following a divine revelation from Iizuna Daimyōjin and invited {{ill|Izuna Gongen|ja|飯縄権現|zh|飯繩權現|qid=Q11666654|lt=Iizuna Daigongen}} to be enshrined on the summit. Tadanetsuna’s son, Moritsuna, also entered the mountain with him, mastered the rites of {{ill|Dakini|ar|داكيني|as|ডাকিনী|az|Dakini|bcl|Dakini|bg|Дакини|bn|ডাকিনী|bo|མཁའ་འགྲོ།|ca|Dakini|cs|Dákiní|de|Dakini|el|Ντακίνι|es|Dakini|et|Daakinid|fa|داکینی|fr|Dakini|hi|डाकिनी|id|Dakini|it|Ḍākinī|ja|荼枳尼天|ka|დაკინი|ko|다키니|lmo|Ḍākinī|ml|ഡാകിനി|mr|डाकिणी|pa|ਡਾਕਿਨੀ|pl|Dakini|pt|Dakini|ru|Дакини|simple|Dakini|sv|Dakini|ta|டாகினி|te|డాకిని|th|ฑากินี|tr|Dakini|uk|Дакіні|vi|Không hành nữ|zh|荼吉尼|qid=Q1127224}}, inherited from his father the Iizuna rites<ref>A unique form of esoteric practice using {{ill|Kuda-gitsune|de|Kuda-kitsune|es|Kuda-gitsune|fr|Kuda-kitsune|id|Kuda-gitsune|ja|管狐|zh|管狐|qid=Q4451648}}</ref>, established the original Iizuna {{ill|ninpō|da|Ninpo|fr|Ninpō|it|Ninpō|ja|忍法|qid=Q3342041}}, styled himself “Sennichi Dayū,” spread {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Iizuna belief}} throughout the country, and became regarded as the progenitor of ninjutsu.

== Genealogy of the Nishina priestly family ==
Below is the genealogy of the Nishina clan, who served for generations as priests of Iizuna Shrine.<ref>Shinano Digital Commons, “(Minochi District) Nishina Clan Genealogy (copy) [https://www.ro-da.jp/shinshu-dcommons/museum_history/03OD0621101700]”</ref> However, their claim to be descendants of {{ill|Taira no Koremori|ar|تايرا نو كوريموري|ca|Taira no Koremori|es|Taira no Koremori|eu|Taira no Koremori|fa|تایرا نو کوره‌موری|fr|Taira no Koremori|it|Taira no Koremori|ja|平維盛|pt|Taira no Koremori|th|ไทระ โนะ โคเรโมริ|zh|平維盛|qid=Q3055506}} is merely self-proclaimed. In reality, it is thought to divide into the line of {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Nishina Morihiro}} – {{ill|Nishina Moriiye|ja|仁科盛家|qid=Q76970446}} – {{ill|Nishina Moritō|ja|仁科盛遠|qid=Q11376460}} – {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Nishina Morikatsu}} (who fell during the {{ill|Jōkyū War|Q1372308|qid=Q1372308}}), and the line beginning with {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Nishina Moritada}}, son of {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Seki Morinaga}} and adopted son of Morikatsu.<ref>Shigeki Kitazawa, *The Nishina Clan*, Tokyo Tosho Shuppankai, 2010</ref>

== The Great Cedar of Sometaruhonomikoto Shrine ==
A natural monument designated by Nagano City. With a height of about 30 meters and a trunk circumference at eye level of 4.82 meters, it is an exceptionally large {{ill|Cryptomeria|Q147388|qid=Q147388|lt=cedar}} even among the shrine grove. Aside from holes made by {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=woodpeckers}}, there is no damage, the tree is vigorous, and its form is fine. It also stands in an appropriate location near the shrine buildings as a sacred tree. Although tall trees in this shrine grove have been struck by lightning several times in the past and damaged one by one, it is fortunate that this great cedar has never been struck by lightning to date.<ref>Partially quoted from Nagano City Board of Education, Cultural Properties Division, “[https://web.archive.org/web/20111221062200/https://www.city.nagano.nagano.jp/uploaded/attachment/5604.pdf#search='Sumetaruhonomikoto' The Great Cedar of Sometaruhonomikoto Shrine]”</ref>.
